summary: Several US outages hit in a few days: the FAA ground stop, United, Apple, Marriott, some banks and reportedly the NSA. Causes are known for only two: a new router at the FAA, and an Apple 'internal update'. Officials say they look unrelated, and Rubio said there is 'zero' information that a malign actor is behind them. US stocks fell on Nov 17 but did not halt, and Bitcoin is down about 12-14% on the week with a calm last day. Telecom, power and geopolitical checks found nothing new, but they were thin this run.

events.title: FAA nationwide ground stop after router overload; router installs paused
events.impact: Flights halted nationwide on Nov 13; about 12,462 flights were cancelled. FAA paused Juniper router installs on Nov 17 and turned off the suspect functions on 60+ routers. FAA NAS feed now shows only weather delays in Florida.
events.stated_cause: FAA says a new router in El Dorado, Arkansas flooded older equipment with data. HPE says its router worked as configured. Root cause is still unknown. DOT brought in the FBI to check for hacking; no hack has been reported.

events.title: United Airlines system outage delays departures
events.impact: A system outage lasting more than 90 minutes delayed United departures on Monday. United said it was resolved.
events.stated_cause: Unknown. Only called a technology issue; no official link to the FAA event.

events.title: Chase and other US banks report outages
events.impact: Chase transactions were disrupted and resumed around 11:49 GMT on Nov 17. Start time is approximate. Reports about other banks come from outage trackers and are not verified.
events.stated_cause: Unknown; described only as a technical issue.

events.title: Apple services (iCloud, Apple Pay, App Store, Support) outage
events.impact: Thousands of Downdetector reports for App Store, iCloud, Apple Pay and Support. Most services recovered by about 20:34 UTC.
events.stated_cause: An Apple spokesperson told CTV the outage was caused by an internal update. The report said nothing suggested an attack.

events.title: Marriott technology issues affect reservations and check-ins
events.impact: Reservations and check-ins were affected, per Downdetector and a live blog. Start time is approximate and I did not see a recovery report.

events.title: NSA reported to have a service disruption
events.impact: Media lists say NSA systems were disrupted. Scope, timing and recovery are unknown; I found no detail from an official source.
events.stated_cause: Unknown. CTV reported there was no suggestion of an attack or that NSA work was affected.

events.title: Platform for business digital tools reports a security incident
events.impact: Only a live-blog headline seen. Company name, scope and impact are unknown to me.
events.stated_cause: Described as a security incident; details unknown.

events.title: US stocks fall for a fourth day; S&P 500 lowest close since July
events.impact: Dow fell 1.64% to 50,759.42, S&P 500 fell 1.03% to 7,340.53 and Nasdaq fell 0.74%. No halts or exchange glitches seen. Futures rose after Nvidia beat estimates.
events.stated_cause: Reports cite worry about AI stock values, interest-rate fears, and caution before Nvidia earnings.

events.title: Bitcoin about 12-14% lower over 7 days, near 64-65K USD
events.impact: Price data shows BTC near 64-65K, down roughly 12-14% on the week but within about 2% over 24 hours. This is a gradual drop, not a sudden crash. No exchange outage found.
events.stated_cause: Not stated in sources checked. One market note mentions pricing in a possible Fed rate hike.

events.title: Cloudflare minor incidents; status shows degraded performance
events.impact: Official status page shows Sites and Services at degraded performance as of 03:57 UTC, plus Amsterdam maintenance. Such notices are frequent, so this is near normal.
events.stated_cause: Earlier notes cited Durable Objects timeouts and regional network issues. No deeper cause published.

events.title: CISA adds actively exploited flaws to its known-exploited list
events.impact: Routine active-exploitation notices (Cisco BroadWorks, Check Point and others). The CISA feed shows routine advisories such as a Siemens ROS# bug. I saw no CISA Emergency Directive.
events.stated_cause: Attackers exploiting software flaws; federal patch deadlines apply. None of these notices is linked to the outages above.

events.title: AWS Middle East regions (UAE, Bahrain) long-running disruption
events.impact: AWS says data in Bahrain and one UAE zone cannot be restored. Most customers moved to other regions. Latest feed updates are dated Sep 15.
events.stated_cause: AWS describes infrastructure damage across several zones; no cause beyond that is given.

connection_assessment.reasoning: The FAA says a new router overloaded older equipment, and Apple says an internal update caused its outage. Nobody has given a cause for United, Marriott, the banks or NSA. No official source links them, and Rubio said there is 'zero' information of a malign actor behind the outages.
connection_assessment.would_change_my_mind: An official statement blaming the same company or attacker, or several big systems failing at the same moment.

alert.reason: Officials see no link between the outages. Stated causes differ, and markets are orderly.

prep_note: Check flight status before travel and keep a little cash or a second payment card handy. Have a backup way to reach your bank. Save key files offline. Use official sources and be wary of viral claims.
